# Adjudication Task — Chapter 285

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃285화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|‘감히 내 제자를!’
  6|
  7|‘당한 만큼 갚아 줬을 뿐입니다. 이것으로 원금은 갚았으니 남은 복리 이자는 우리 길드 수뇌부와 상의해 보시고요.’
  8|
  9|‘……네놈.’
 10|
 11|‘승낙하신 것으로 알겠습니다.’
 12|
 13|‘오늘 일은…… 절대 잊지 않겠다.’
 14|
 15|
 16|
 17|불과 몇 분 전 나누었던 대화다.
 18|
 19|이정룡은 살기가 뚝뚝 떨어지는 그 한마디를 남기고 자리를 떴다.
 20|
 21|그가 지니고 있던 포션으로 응급 처치는 했지만, 박지훈이 입은 부상은 포션만으로는 치유할 수 없을 정도로 깊었다. 자신의 제자가 그 꼴이 되었으니 마음이 급했을 것이다.
 22|
 23|“휴.”
 24|
 25|저 멀리 느껴지던 이정룡의 인기척이 완전히 사라지자, 절로 안도의 한숨이 흘러나왔다.
 26|
 27|“어이고, 힘들다.”
 28|
 29|마지막까지 붙들고 있던 긴장의 끈을 놓자 맥이 탁 풀린다.
 30|
 31|피곤하다. 이정룡과의 격돌로 약간의 내상을 입긴 했지만, 그보다는 정신적인 피로감이 더 컸다.
 32|
 33|‘사고 하나 제대로 쳤네.’
 34|
 35|나는 오늘, 세계에서도 인정받는 S급 헌터와 초대형 길드를 적으로 돌렸다.
 36|
 37|까마득한 절벽을 무대로 한 아슬아슬한 외줄 타기.
 38|
 39|나와 이정룡은 외줄의 한가운데에서 만났고 결국 물러난 것은 저쪽이었다.
 40|
 41|‘어쩔 수 없었겠지. 난 그 부분을 정확히 파고든 거고.’
 42|
 43|잃을 것이 많은 사람은 위험을 두려워하기 마련이다.
 44|
 45|이정룡이라는, 아레스 길드라는 호랑이가 쓰러지면 산군(山君)이 갖고 있던 명예는 땅에 떨어지고 사체는 숲속 동물들, 즉 경쟁자들의 훌륭한 먹이가 될 것이다.
 46|
 47|‘물론 깔끔하게 해결할 방법은 살인멸구(殺人滅口)였겠지만…….’
 48|
 49|이정룡은 알고 있다. 내가 그리 호락호락한 상대가 아님을.
 50|
 51|한 번의 격돌로 자신이 우위에 있음을 확인했지만, 눈앞의 늑대가 제법 위협적인 상대라는 사실을 깨닫기에는 충분했을 것이다.
 52|
 53|나는 입가에 묻은 피를 문지르며 생각했다.
 54|
 55|‘세 걸음.’
 56|
 57|오늘 이정룡을 상대로 나는 세 걸음을 물러났다.
 58|
 59|하지만 오늘의 세 걸음은 곧 두 걸음이 될 것이고, 머지않아 두 걸음은 한 걸음으로 좁혀질 것이다.
 60|
 61|그리고 이다음은…….
 62|
 63|‘내가 당신을 뛰어넘을 거야.’
 64|
 65|이정룡에게 말했던, 늑대가 호랑이를 일대일로 이기는 다큐멘터리 따위는 본 적 없다.
 66|
 67|하지만 내게는 끝없이 성장할 수 있는 잠재력이 있다. 마치 잠룡(潛龍)이라는 별호처럼.
 68|
 69|‘그때가 되면 나도, 우리 길드도 당신이 생각했던 것 이상으로 강해져 있을 거다.’
 70|
 71|이번 일로 이룬 것은 임꺽정의 복수뿐만이 아니다. 평화 길드를 성장시킬 절호의 기회를 얻었다.
 72|
 73|처음 블랙 헌터의 습격에 겁먹고 물러났다면 평화 길드는 그저 그런 중견 길드로 남았을 테지만, 맞섰기에 복수와 보상을 얻었고 이후의 일은 최 팀장의 역량에 달렸다.
 74|
 75|‘그 사람이라면 잘 해낼 거야.’
 76|
 77|문득 몇 시간 전, 최 팀장과 나누었던 대화가 떠올랐다.
 78|
 79|
 80|
 81|‘무슨 일을 벌일 생각입니까?’
 82|
 83|‘글쎄요. 제 짐작이 맞으면 눈깔이 뒤집혀서 무슨 짓을 할지 모르겠는데.’
 84|
 85|‘혹시 명동 길드에라도 쳐들어갈 생각입니까?’
 86|
 87|‘아니라고 장담은 못 하겠네요.’
 88|
 89|
 90|
 91|내 말을 들은 송송이는 미쳤다고 했고, 김 집사는 말없이 바라보기만 했다.
 92|
 93|하지만 최 팀장은 달랐다.
 94|
 95|그가 한 말은 내 예상을 훌쩍 뛰어넘는 것이었다.
 96|
 97|
 98|
 99|‘그럼 가십시오.’
100|
101|‘네?’
102|
103|‘명동 길드. 가서 때려 부수고 한바탕 엎어 놓으세요. 아, 그렇다고 서울 한복판에서 빌딩 무너트리고 사람 죽이란 말은 아닙니다. 자칫하다가는 교도소가 길드 하우스가 될 테니까요.’
104|
105|‘……말리실 줄 알았는데요.’
106|
107|‘말렸을 겁니다, 진태경 씨가 아니었다면. 어떻게든 머리를 쥐어짜 다른 방법을 모색했겠죠.’
108|
109|‘그런데 왜.’
110|
111|‘진태경 씨는 언뜻 보면 무모해 보이지만, 항상 최악의 상황을 염두에 두고 움직이는 사람입니다. 그리고 늘 최선의 결과를 갖고 오죠.’
112|
113|‘정말, 괜찮겠습니까?’
114|
115|‘저는 평화 길드를 세계 최고로 키울 생각입니다. 길드원이 습격을 받은 상황에서 물러난다면 절대 세계 최고가 될 수 없어요.’
116|
117|‘그럼 정말로…….’
118|
119|‘하십시오. 어떤 결과가 나오든 제가 책임집니다.’
120|
121|
122|
123|최 팀장이 건넨 마지막 말이 귓가에 생생하게 울려 퍼지는 듯했다.
124|
125|
126|
127|‘전 진태경 씨를 믿습니다. 어쩌면 저 자신보다 더.’
128|
129|
130|
131|나는 그가 보내 준 무한한 신뢰에 보답했다.
132|
133|임꺽정이 당했던 것 이상을 박지훈에게 돌려주었고, 감히 범접할 수 없는 적들을 상대로 사과와 보상을 암묵적으로 약속받았다.
134|
135|‘세계 최고의 길드라.’
136|
137|최 팀장의 당찬 포부를 떠올리자 피식 웃음이 새어 나온다.
138|
139|나는 핸드폰을 꺼내 전화를 걸었다.
140|
141|신호가 가기 무섭게 한 사람이 전화를 받았다.
142|
143|- 네. 최민우입니다.
144|
145|최 팀장. 바로 그다.
146|
147|“드릴 말씀이 많은데. 어디로 가면 될까요?”
148|
149|- 진태경 씨! 살아 있었군요!
150|
151|“……?”
152|
153|- 죽은 줄 알았습니다. 정말 진태경 씨 맞습니까?
154|
155|“…….”
156|
157|너 자신보다 믿는다며, 이 개새끼야…….
158|
159|
160|
161|* * *
162|
163|
164|
165|“지훈아! 정신 차리거라!”
166|
167|어린 제자를 향한 스승의 절절한 외침과 다급한 발걸음.
168|
169|이정룡의 뒤를 바짝 따라가던 명동 길드장 박태섭은 놀란 눈빛으로 그의 뒷모습을 바라봤다.
170|
171|‘이정룡에게 이런 면모가 있었나?’
172|
173|그는 오랜 세월 이정룡을 지켜봤다.
174|
175|대격변 당시에는 어쩐지 모르게 다가가기 힘든 사람이라고만 생각했다.
176|
177|그러나 종전 후 아레스 길드가 세워지고 이정룡이 실권을 휘어잡으면서 그의 진면목을 똑똑히 알 수 있었다.
178|
179|강철처럼 단단하고, 독사처럼 은밀하며, 남들이 몸서리칠 만 한 일들을 스스럼없이 행한다.
180|
181|박태섭의 시선에서 바라본 이정룡은 그런 인물이었다. 적으로도, 아군으로도 만나고 싶지 않은 자.
182|
183|‘저자도 결국은 사람이었군.’
184|
185|그러나 박태섭이 느낀 묘한 감흥은, 긴 복도를 빠져나와 홀로 들어선 순간 흔적도 없이 사라졌다.
186|
187|“오셨습니까.”
188|
189|“……!”
190|
191|중년의 사내였다. 군인처럼 절도 있는 행동. 극도로 단련된 육체는 입고 있는 검은색 정장으로도 가릴 수 없다.
192|
193|그의 뒤에 철탑처럼 서 있는 이십 명의 남녀 또한 마찬가지였다. 그들의 가슴께에는 아레스 길드를 뜻하는 엠블럼이 박혀 있었다.
194|
195|‘기척도 느끼지 못했는데.’
196|
197|박태섭의 충격은 그뿐만이 아니었다.
198|
199|중년 사내의 어깨너머, 쓰러져 있는 백여 명의 명동 길드원들을 발견한 그가 눈을 부릅떴다.
200|
201|“이게 무슨……!”
202|
203|중년 사내가 건조한 목소리로 대답했다.
204|
205|“수면 마법으로 재웠을 뿐입니다. 아직까지는요.”
206|
207|아직까지는.
208|
209|의미심장한 말이다. 지금은 마법의 힘으로 잠들어 있을 뿐이지만, 영원히 잠들 수도 있다는 뜻이기도 했다.
210|
211|대노한 박태섭이 고함을 지르려던 찰나였다.
212|
213|“무슨 문제라도 있나?”
214|
215|이정룡의 신형이 서서히 돌아섰다. 그리고 그의 얼굴을 마주한 박태섭은 자신이 커다란 착각을 했음을 깨달았다.
216|
217|‘전부 연기였어.’
218|
219|어떤 감정도 떠올라 있지 않은 무표정한 얼굴과 깊게 가라앉은 눈빛. 다급한 발걸음과 제자의 안위를 걱정하던 절절한 외침 따위는 찾아볼 수 없다.
220|
221|서늘한 한기가 박태섭의 등줄기를 타고 스멀스멀 기어올랐다.
222|
223|“이보게, 박 길드장.”
224|
225|부드러운 목소리에 숨은 칼날이 느껴진다. 독사의 혀가 움직일 때마다 독이 흘러나오는 듯했다.
226|
227|“20년쯤 전인가. 어느 날 자네가 나를 찾아와 대뜸 무릎을 꿇었었지.”
228|
229|“……!”
230|
231|“아직 기억하고 있나?”
232|
233|“……물론입니다.”
234|
235|박태섭은 이를 악물었다.
236|
237|어찌 기억하지 못하겠는가. 벌써 20년이 되어 가는 일이지만 그때 느낀 절박함은 뼛속 깊이 남아 있었다.
238|
239|연이은 대규모 사업 실패, 엄청난 액수의 빚과 실패자를 바라보는 듯한 사람들의 눈빛…….
240|
241|그것은 박태섭에게 있어 대격변보다 끔찍한 생지옥이었다.
242|
243|주변인들에게 수많은 거절을 당한 끝에 찾아간 사람이 바로 이정룡이다.
244|
245|그는 무릎 꿇은 박태섭을 물끄러미 바라보다가 한 가지 질문을 던졌다.
246|
247|
248|
249|‘내가 돕는다면, 자네는 날 위해서 무엇을 해 줄 수 있지?’
250|
251|
252|
253|박태섭의 대답에는 망설임이 없었다.
254|
255|
256|
257|‘무엇이든 하겠습니다.’
258|
259|‘그거 마음에 드는군.’
260|
261|
262|
263|만약 그 말을 하지 않았더라면 어떻게 됐을까?
264|
265|지난 20년간 수백, 수천 번도 넘게 스스로에게 질문해 봤지만 의미 없는 일이다. 이미 돌아가기에는 너무 먼 길을 왔다.
266|
267|대가 없는 호의는 없었고 이정룡을 위해 온갖 범법 행위를 일삼아야 했다.
268|
269|문득 정신을 차리고 보니 목줄을 잡힌 채 끌려가는 자신의 모습이 보일 뿐이었다.
270|
271|“요즘 박 길드장을 보면 부쩍 그런 생각이 든단 말이지. 그때 날 찾아와서 했던 말들이 전부 속 빈 강정처럼 느껴져.”
272|
273|“그럴 리가 있겠습니까.”
274|
275|“아니야. 사람이라는 동물이 원래 그래. 은혜를 입어도 감사하는 마음은 금세 잊고 불평만 쌓여 가지. 얼어 죽을 뻔한 놈을 살려 놔도 모닥불 쬐면 생각이 바뀌니, 이거 원. 하하.”
276|
277|“…….”
278|
279|말려 올라간 입꼬리와는 달리 이정룡의 눈빛은 얼음장처럼 차가웠다.
280|
281|박태섭이 굳은 얼굴로 고개를 숙였을 때, 한층 누그러진 목소리가 이어졌다.
282|
283|“앞으로도 계속 잘해 보자는 의미에서 한 말일세. 자네 길드원들도 무사할 테니 아무런 걱정하지 말고. 안 그런가, 석 팀장?”
284|
285|이정룡의 경호를 맡고 있는 중년의 사내, 석 팀장이 무미건조한 목소리로 대답했다.
286|
287|“물론입니다.”
288|
289|“자, 그럼 나는 이만 가 봐야겠네. 다음에 또 보세.”
290|
291|툭툭.
292|
293|박태섭은 딱딱하게 굳은 채 자신의 어깨를 두드려 주고 떠나는 이정룡의 뒷모습을 바라보았다.
294|
295|
296|
297|* * *
298|
299|
300|
301|내려가는 엘리베이터 안에서 석 팀장이 입을 열었다.
302|
303|“처리할까요?”
304|
305|“누구? 아, 박태섭이.”
306|
307|“네. 표정이 불안불안 하더군요.”
308|
309|“그 친구는 생각이 얼굴에 다 드러나. 처음 몇 년 정도는 고분고분하더니 등 따시고 배부르니까 슬슬 다른 생각이 드는 게지.”
310|
311|“너무 많이 알고 있습니다. 이번 일도 너무 허술하게 처리해서 부길드장님께 불똥이 튀었고요.”
312|
313|처음으로 석 팀장의 목소리에 감정이 깃들었다. 바로 분노다.
314|

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

—I thought you were dead. Is this really Jin Taekyung?

[P70]
“…….”

[P71]
*You said you trusted me more than yourself, you son of a bitch…*

[P72]
* * *

[P73]
“Jihoon! Wake up!”

[P74]
A master’s anguished cry for his young Disciple rang out alongside hurried footsteps.

[P75]
Park Tae Seop, the Guild Master of Myeongdong Guild, followed close behind Lee Jungryong and stared at his back in surprise.

[P76]
*Did Lee Jungryong have this side to him?*

[P77]
Park Tae Seop had watched Lee Jungryong for many years.

[P78]
During the Great Cataclysm, he had merely thought of him as someone who was strangely difficult to approach.

[P79]
But after the war ended and Ares Guild was established, Lee Jungryong seized real power within it. Only then did Park Tae Seop come to understand his true nature.

[P80]
Hard as steel. Sly as a viper. A man who committed acts that would make others shudder without the slightest hesitation.

[P81]
That was Lee Jungryong in Park Tae Seop’s eyes—a man he never wanted to face as either an enemy or an ally.

[P82]
*So he’s human after all.*

[P83]
But that strange sense of wonder vanished without a trace the moment they emerged from the long corridor and entered the hall.

[P84]
“Welcome.”

[P85]
“……!”

[P86]
The speaker was a middle-aged man. His movements were as crisp and disciplined as a soldier’s, and even his black suit couldn’t conceal his supremely trained physique.

[P87]
The same was true of the twenty men and women standing behind him like iron towers. Each wore the emblem of Ares Guild over their chest.

[P88]
*I didn’t sense any of them.*

[P89]
That wasn’t the only shock awaiting Park Tae Seop.

[P90]
He looked past the middle-aged man and spotted roughly a hundred Myeongdong Guild members sprawled across the floor. His eyes widened.

[P91]
“What is the meaning of this…?”

[P92]
The middle-aged man answered in a dry voice.

[P93]
“We merely put them to sleep with magic. For now.”

[P94]
*For now.*

[P95]
The words carried a clear implication. At the moment, they were merely asleep under the influence of magic.

[P96]
But they could just as easily be put to sleep forever.

[P97]
Park Tae Seop was about to shout in fury when—

[P98]
“Is there a problem?”

[P99]
Lee Jungryong slowly turned around.

[P100]
The instant Park Tae Seop saw his face, he realized how gravely mistaken he had been.

[P101]
*It was all an act.*

[P102]
Lee Jungryong’s face was devoid of emotion, his eyes deep and cold. There was no trace of his hurried footsteps or the anguished cries of a master fearing for his Disciple’s life.

[P103]
An icy chill crept up Park Tae Seop’s spine.

[P104]
“Guild Master Park.”

[P105]
A blade lay hidden within Lee Jungryong’s gentle voice. It was as though venom dripped from the viper’s tongue with every word.

[P106]
“Was it about twenty years ago? One day, you came to me and dropped to your knees without warning.”

[P107]
“……!”

[P108]
“Do you still remember?”

[P109]
“……Of course.”

[P110]
Park Tae Seop clenched his teeth.

[P111]
How could he possibly forget? Nearly twenty years had passed, but the desperation he’d felt then remained etched into his bones.

[P112]
A string of failed business ventures. A staggering mountain of debt. The way people looked at him as though he were a failure…

[P113]
To Park Tae Seop, it had been a living hell worse than the Great Cataclysm.

[P114]
After being turned away by countless acquaintances, he had finally sought out Lee Jungryong.

[P115]
Lee Jungryong had gazed down at the kneeling Park Tae Seop and asked him a single question.

[P116]
*If I help you, what will you do for me?*

[P117]
Park Tae Seop had answered without hesitation.

[P118]
*Anything.*

[P119]
*I like that answer.*

[P120]
What would have happened if he hadn’t said those words?

[P121]
He had asked himself that question hundreds, even thousands of times over the past twenty years, but it was meaningless. He had already come too far to turn back.

[P122]
No favor came without a price, and he had been forced to commit every manner of crime for Lee Jungryong.

[P123]
By the time he came to his senses, he was already being dragged along by a leash around his neck.

[P124]
“Whenever I look at you these days, Guild Master Park, I can’t help thinking about that day. Everything you said when you came to me back then is beginning to sound hollow.”

[P125]
“How could that be?”

[P126]
“No, that’s simply human nature. No matter how much someone owes you, they soon forget their gratitude and begin piling up complaints. Save a man from freezing to death, and he changes his tune the moment he warms himself by the fire. What can you do? Ha ha.”

[P127]
“…….”

[P128]
Despite the upward curl of his lips, Lee Jungryong’s eyes were as cold as ice.

[P129]
When Park Tae Seop lowered his head, his expression rigid, Lee Jungryong continued in a gentler voice.

[P130]
“I only brought it up because I hope we’ll continue working well together. Your Guild members will be perfectly safe, so don’t worry. Isn’t that right, Team Leader Seok?”

[P131]
The middle-aged man responsible for Lee Jungryong’s security, Team Leader Seok, answered in a flat voice.

[P132]
“Of course.”

[P133]
“Well, I should be on my way. I’ll see you again.”

[P134]
Pat, pat.

[P135]
Park Tae Seop stood frozen as Lee Jungryong patted him on the shoulder and walked away.

[P136]
* * *

[P137]
Inside the descending elevator, Team Leader Seok spoke.

[P138]
“Shall I take care of him?”

[P139]
“Who? Ah, Park Tae Seop.”

[P140]
“Yes. The look on his face made me uneasy.”

[P141]
“That man’s every thought shows on his face. He was obedient enough for the first few years, but once he got warm and well-fed, he began entertaining other ideas.”

[P142]
“He knows too much. He also handled this incident so poorly that the fallout reached you, Vice Guild Master.”

[P143]
For the first time, emotion entered Team Leader Seok’s voice.

[P144]
Anger.

[P145]
Seeing the man’s unwavering loyalty, Lee Jungryong smiled faintly.

[P146]
“Leave him alone for now. We’ve only just started tasting the dish. Of course it’s still bland.”

[P147]
“Excuse me?”

[P148]
At that moment, the elevator doors opened with a ding.

[P149]
Lee Jungryong continued as he walked.

[P150]
“I’m saying I only gave them a little prod. I wanted to see how they would react.”

[P151]
“Then…?”

[P152]
“You occasionally underestimate me. If I had truly set my mind to it, would I have entrusted the job to half-baked fools like them?”

[P153]
Team Leader Seok let out a low exclamation.

[P154]
“You anticipated all of this.”

[P155]
“I’ve barely taken a single spoonful to taste it. If it doesn’t suit my palate, I can always add some salt and pepper.”

[P156]
“As expected of you, Vice Guild Master.”

[P157]
Lee Jungryong smiled gently at the admiration in Team Leader Seok’s eyes.

[P158]
But his true thoughts were different. There was something he couldn’t reveal even to Team Leader Seok, his right-hand man.

[P159]
*Jin Taekyung is no ordinary bastard.*

[P160]
From the beginning, it had been the Peace Guild that bothered Lee Jungryong, not Jin Taekyung.

[P161]
Even if he had personally intervened, he couldn’t guarantee that something like this wouldn’t have happened. After all, he wasn’t the sort of man who used a cleaver meant for cattle to kill a chicken.

[P162]
It was certainly efficient, but if an unforeseen variable appeared, the entire plan could go awry.

[P163]
*Who would’ve thought there was a wolf hiding among the chickens?*

[P164]
Lee Jungryong rubbed his tingling wrist.

[P165]
For a moment, he had felt tremendous heat and power from the brat. It had been far too strong to dismiss as a mere trick from some green youngster.

[P166]
*He knew how to control mana properly. Where could a man who was only an F-rank Hunter until recently have learned…?*

[P167]
He did have a fairly good idea.

[P168]
After finishing that thought, Lee Jungryong addressed Team Leader Seok.

[P169]
“Keep a close eye on Jin Taekyung.”

[P170]
“Don’t worry. If he becomes a nuisance, I’ll deal with him personally.”

[P171]
Team Leader Seok had always been reliable. He was a born fighting prodigy and the finest of all the youths Lee Jungryong had personally selected and trained. His skill was beyond question. Even a high-level ranker like Park Tae Seop was no match for him.

[P172]
But a question suddenly occurred to Lee Jungryong.

[P173]
Could Team Leader Seok really defeat Jin Taekyung?

[P174]
“Team Leader Seok. No, Go Jun.”

[P175]
His form of address had shifted from the man’s position to his name.

[P176]
Team Leader Seok understood the meaning immediately. If he had lacked even that much perception, he could never have become Lee Jungryong’s prized Disciple.

[P177]
“Yes, Master.”

[P178]
“Hmm. It’s nothing. I entertained an absurd thought for a moment.”

[P179]
Lee Jungryong clicked his tongue softly and walked through the main entrance.

[P180]
Five men and women were waiting outside the building, dressed in robes covered with elaborate patterns and carrying staffs.

[P181]
“We greet the Vice Guild Master.”

[P182]
“Those outfits are certainly gaudy. Can’t you dress a little more ordinarily?”

[P183]
“They’ll look ordinary to everyone else.”

[P184]
They were A-rank mages under Lee Jungryong’s direct command.

[P185]
Just as the oldest-looking mage had said, not one of the hundreds of people hurrying along the sidewalk paid them any attention.

[P186]
None of those people even knew that an incredible battle had taken place directly above them—one that had nearly brought down a high-rise building.

[P187]
“This is why magic is so convenient.”

[P188]
The mages had used brute force to blanket everything within a radius of roughly two hundred meters with illusion magic. Only the handpicked A-rank mages of Ares Guild could pull off something on that scale.

[P189]
They would remain there and maintain the illusion until the entire aftermath had been dealt with.

[P190]
“Good. Use that convenient magic of yours to make sure no rumors get out. If anyone looks dangerous, use mental magic to tamper with their memories.”

[P191]
“Yes, sir. Understood. But that man is badly injured.”

[P192]
“Ah, him?”

[P193]
Lee Jungryong glanced at Park Jihoon, who was being carried on the back of a Hunter from his security team, and casually tossed out an order.

[P194]
“Treat him just enough to keep him alive, then dump him somewhere.”

[P195]
If he died, so be it. Even if he recovered, he would never again be able to display half his current strength.

[P196]
Lee Jungryong had no interest in collecting spent batteries. He already had countless others. All he had to do was replace this one.

[P197]
*Still, he was useful at the end.*

[P198]
Through Park Jihoon, Lee Jungryong had confirmed the extent of Jin Taekyung’s ruthlessness.

[P199]
Once blood had been spilled, he should have killed him. Lee Jungryong would certainly have done so.

[P200]
*You couldn’t take that final step.*

[P201]
What did it matter if he cut off both arms and carved the man’s body to pieces? As long as his enemy still drew breath, it wasn’t complete revenge.

[P202]
It was nothing more than venting his anger.

[P203]
*That half-measure will come back to poison you someday.*

[P204]
Lee Jungryong let out a derisive chuckle and climbed into the waiting car.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 285

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃285화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|‘감히 내 제자를!’
  6|
  7|‘당한 만큼 갚아 줬을 뿐입니다. 이것으로 원금은 갚았으니 남은 복리 이자는 우리 길드 수뇌부와 상의해 보시고요.’
  8|
  9|‘……네놈.’
 10|
 11|‘승낙하신 것으로 알겠습니다.’
 12|
 13|‘오늘 일은…… 절대 잊지 않겠다.’
 14|
 15|
 16|
 17|불과 몇 분 전 나누었던 대화다.
 18|
 19|이정룡은 살기가 뚝뚝 떨어지는 그 한마디를 남기고 자리를 떴다.
 20|
 21|그가 지니고 있던 포션으로 응급 처치는 했지만, 박지훈이 입은 부상은 포션만으로는 치유할 수 없을 정도로 깊었다. 자신의 제자가 그 꼴이 되었으니 마음이 급했을 것이다.
 22|
 23|“휴.”
 24|
 25|저 멀리 느껴지던 이정룡의 인기척이 완전히 사라지자, 절로 안도의 한숨이 흘러나왔다.
 26|
 27|“어이고, 힘들다.”
 28|
 29|마지막까지 붙들고 있던 긴장의 끈을 놓자 맥이 탁 풀린다.
 30|
 31|피곤하다. 이정룡과의 격돌로 약간의 내상을 입긴 했지만, 그보다는 정신적인 피로감이 더 컸다.
 32|
 33|‘사고 하나 제대로 쳤네.’
 34|
 35|나는 오늘, 세계에서도 인정받는 S급 헌터와 초대형 길드를 적으로 돌렸다.
 36|
 37|까마득한 절벽을 무대로 한 아슬아슬한 외줄 타기.
 38|
 39|나와 이정룡은 외줄의 한가운데에서 만났고 결국 물러난 것은 저쪽이었다.
 40|
 41|‘어쩔 수 없었겠지. 난 그 부분을 정확히 파고든 거고.’
 42|
 43|잃을 것이 많은 사람은 위험을 두려워하기 마련이다.
 44|
 45|이정룡이라는, 아레스 길드라는 호랑이가 쓰러지면 산군(山君)이 갖고 있던 명예는 땅에 떨어지고 사체는 숲속 동물들, 즉 경쟁자들의 훌륭한 먹이가 될 것이다.
 46|
 47|‘물론 깔끔하게 해결할 방법은 살인멸구(殺人滅口)였겠지만…….’
 48|
 49|이정룡은 알고 있다. 내가 그리 호락호락한 상대가 아님을.
 50|
 51|한 번의 격돌로 자신이 우위에 있음을 확인했지만, 눈앞의 늑대가 제법 위협적인 상대라는 사실을 깨닫기에는 충분했을 것이다.
 52|
 53|나는 입가에 묻은 피를 문지르며 생각했다.
 54|
 55|‘세 걸음.’
 56|
 57|오늘 이정룡을 상대로 나는 세 걸음을 물러났다.
 58|
 59|하지만 오늘의 세 걸음은 곧 두 걸음이 될 것이고, 머지않아 두 걸음은 한 걸음으로 좁혀질 것이다.
 60|
 61|그리고 이다음은…….
 62|
 63|‘내가 당신을 뛰어넘을 거야.’
 64|
 65|이정룡에게 말했던, 늑대가 호랑이를 일대일로 이기는 다큐멘터리 따위는 본 적 없다.
 66|
 67|하지만 내게는 끝없이 성장할 수 있는 잠재력이 있다. 마치 잠룡(潛龍)이라는 별호처럼.
 68|
 69|‘그때가 되면 나도, 우리 길드도 당신이 생각했던 것 이상으로 강해져 있을 거다.’
 70|
 71|이번 일로 이룬 것은 임꺽정의 복수뿐만이 아니다. 평화 길드를 성장시킬 절호의 기회를 얻었다.
 72|
 73|처음 블랙 헌터의 습격에 겁먹고 물러났다면 평화 길드는 그저 그런 중견 길드로 남았을 테지만, 맞섰기에 복수와 보상을 얻었고 이후의 일은 최 팀장의 역량에 달렸다.
 74|
 75|‘그 사람이라면 잘 해낼 거야.’
 76|
 77|문득 몇 시간 전, 최 팀장과 나누었던 대화가 떠올랐다.
 78|
 79|
 80|
 81|‘무슨 일을 벌일 생각입니까?’
 82|
 83|‘글쎄요. 제 짐작이 맞으면 눈깔이 뒤집혀서 무슨 짓을 할지 모르겠는데.’
 84|
 85|‘혹시 명동 길드에라도 쳐들어갈 생각입니까?’
 86|
 87|‘아니라고 장담은 못 하겠네요.’
 88|
 89|
 90|
 91|내 말을 들은 송송이는 미쳤다고 했고, 김 집사는 말없이 바라보기만 했다.
 92|
 93|하지만 최 팀장은 달랐다.
 94|
 95|그가 한 말은 내 예상을 훌쩍 뛰어넘는 것이었다.
 96|
 97|
 98|
 99|‘그럼 가십시오.’
100|
101|‘네?’
102|
103|‘명동 길드. 가서 때려 부수고 한바탕 엎어 놓으세요. 아, 그렇다고 서울 한복판에서 빌딩 무너트리고 사람 죽이란 말은 아닙니다. 자칫하다가는 교도소가 길드 하우스가 될 테니까요.’
104|
105|‘……말리실 줄 알았는데요.’
106|
107|‘말렸을 겁니다, 진태경 씨가 아니었다면. 어떻게든 머리를 쥐어짜 다른 방법을 모색했겠죠.’
108|
109|‘그런데 왜.’
110|
111|‘진태경 씨는 언뜻 보면 무모해 보이지만, 항상 최악의 상황을 염두에 두고 움직이는 사람입니다. 그리고 늘 최선의 결과를 갖고 오죠.’
112|
113|‘정말, 괜찮겠습니까?’
114|
115|‘저는 평화 길드를 세계 최고로 키울 생각입니다. 길드원이 습격을 받은 상황에서 물러난다면 절대 세계 최고가 될 수 없어요.’
116|
117|‘그럼 정말로…….’
118|
119|‘하십시오. 어떤 결과가 나오든 제가 책임집니다.’
120|
121|
122|
123|최 팀장이 건넨 마지막 말이 귓가에 생생하게 울려 퍼지는 듯했다.
124|
125|
126|
127|‘전 진태경 씨를 믿습니다. 어쩌면 저 자신보다 더.’
128|
129|
130|
131|나는 그가 보내 준 무한한 신뢰에 보답했다.
132|
133|임꺽정이 당했던 것 이상을 박지훈에게 돌려주었고, 감히 범접할 수 없는 적들을 상대로 사과와 보상을 암묵적으로 약속받았다.
134|
135|‘세계 최고의 길드라.’
136|
137|최 팀장의 당찬 포부를 떠올리자 피식 웃음이 새어 나온다.
138|
139|나는 핸드폰을 꺼내 전화를 걸었다.
140|
141|신호가 가기 무섭게 한 사람이 전화를 받았다.
142|
143|- 네. 최민우입니다.
144|
145|최 팀장. 바로 그다.
146|
147|“드릴 말씀이 많은데. 어디로 가면 될까요?”
148|
149|- 진태경 씨! 살아 있었군요!
150|
151|“……?”
152|
153|- 죽은 줄 알았습니다. 정말 진태경 씨 맞습니까?
154|
155|“…….”
156|
157|너 자신보다 믿는다며, 이 개새끼야…….
158|
159|
160|
161|* * *
162|
163|
164|
165|“지훈아! 정신 차리거라!”
166|

[P24]

[P35]

*He’ll handle it well.*

[P38]
“What are you planning to do?”

[P39]
“Hard to say. If my hunch is right, I might see red, and even I don’t know what I’ll do.”

[P40]
“Are you thinking of storming Myeongdong Guild?”

[P41]
“I can’t promise I’m not.”

[P42]
Song Song had called me crazy after hearing that, while Butler Kim had only stared at me in silence.

[P43]
But Team Leader Choi had been different.

[P44]
What he said had gone far beyond anything I expected.

[P45]
“Then go.”

[P46]
“Excuse me?”

[P47]
“Myeongdong Guild. Go there, smash the place up, and turn it upside down. Ah, I’m not telling you to collapse a building in the middle of Seoul and kill people. If you’re not careful, the prison will become the Guild house.”

[P48]
“……I thought you were going to stop me.”

[P49]
“I would have, if you weren’t Jin Taekyung. I would have racked my brain and looked for another way somehow.”

[P50]
“Then why?”

[P51]
“Jin Taekyung, you may look reckless at first glance, but you always move with the worst possible situation in mind. And you always bring back the best possible result.”

[P52]
“Are you really sure this is all right?”

[P53]
“I intend to make the Peace Guild the greatest Guild in the world. If we back down when one of our Guild members has been attacked, we can never become the best in the world.”

[P54]
“Then you really want me to…”

[P55]
“Do it. Whatever the result, I’ll take responsibility.”

[P56]
Team Leader Choi’s final words seemed to ring vividly in my ears.

[P57]
“I trust Jin Taekyung. Perhaps more than I trust myself.”

[P58]
I had repaid the boundless trust he had placed in me.

[P59]
I had given Park Jihoon more than Im Kkeokjeong had suffered, and I had tacitly secured apologies and compensation from enemies no one could dare approach.

[P60]
*The greatest Guild in the world, huh?*

[P61]
Remembering Team Leader Choi’s bold ambition, I let out a quiet laugh.

[P62]
I took out my phone and made a call.

[P63]
Someone answered before the phone had even had time to ring properly.

[P64]
—Yes. This is Choi Minwoo.

[P65]
Team Leader Choi. It was him.

[P66]
“I have a lot to tell you. Where should I go?”

[P67]
—Jin Taekyung! You’re alive!

[P68]
“……?”

[P69]
—I thought you were dead. Is this really Jin Taekyung?

[P70]
“…….”

[P71]
*You said you trusted me more than yourself, you son of a bitch…*

[P73]
“Jihoon! Wake up!”

[P74]

[P75]

*Did Lee Jungryong have this side to him?*

[P77]
Park Tae Seop had watched Lee Jungryong for many years.

[P78]
During the Great Cataclysm, he had simply thought of him as someone who was strangely difficult to approach.

[P79]

[P80]
He was as hard as steel, as secretive as a viper, and capable of doing things that would make other people shudder without hesitation.

[P81]
That was the kind of man Lee Jungryong was in Park Tae Seop’s eyes—a person he never wanted to meet as either an enemy or an ally.

[P82]
*So he was a human being after all.*

[P83]
But the strange impression Park Tae Seop had felt vanished without a trace the moment they emerged from the long corridor and entered the hall.

[P84]
“Welcome.”

[P85]
“……!”

[P86]
The speaker was a middle-aged man. His movements were as precise as a soldier’s. His extremely well-trained body could not be concealed even by the black suit he wore.

[P87]
The same was true of the twenty men and women standing behind him like iron towers. An emblem symbolizing Ares Guild was fixed over each of their chests.

[P88]
*I didn’t even sense their presence.*

[P89]
That wasn’t the only thing that shocked Park Tae Seop.

[P90]
Over the middle-aged man’s shoulder, he spotted roughly a hundred Myeongdong Guild members lying collapsed on the floor. His eyes widened.

[P91]
“What is the meaning of this…?”

[P92]
The middle-aged man answered in a dry voice.

[P93]
“We merely put them to sleep with sleep magic. For now.”

[P94]
*For now.*

[P95]
It was a meaningful choice of words. They were only asleep under the power of magic at present, but it also meant they could remain asleep forever.

[P96]
Park Tae Seop was just about to shout in fury when—

[P97]
“Is there some problem?”

[P98]
Lee Jungryong slowly turned around.

[P99]
The moment Park Tae Seop saw his face, he realized that he had been profoundly mistaken.

[P100]
*It had all been an act.*

[P101]
There was no emotion on Lee Jungryong’s expression, and his eyes were sunk deep and cold. There was no trace of the hurried footsteps or anguished cries worrying over his Disciple’s safety.

[P102]
An icy chill slowly crept up Park Tae Seop’s spine.

[P103]
“Guild Master Park.”

[P104]
There was a blade hidden in Lee Jungryong’s gentle voice. It was as though venom dripped from the viper’s tongue every time it moved.

[P105]
“Was it about twenty years ago? One day, you came to me and abruptly dropped to your knees.”

[P106]
“……!”

[P107]
“Do you still remember?”

[P108]
“……Of course.”

[P109]
Park Tae Seop clenched his teeth.

[P110]
How could he not remember? Nearly twenty years had passed, but the desperation he had felt back then remained buried deep in his bones.

[P111]
A string of massive business failures, debts totaling an enormous sum, and the looks people gave him as though they were staring at a failure…

[P112]
For Park Tae Seop, it had been a living hell more horrifying than the Great Cataclysm.

[P113]
After being rejected countless times by the people around him, the person he had gone to was Lee Jungryong.

[P114]
Lee Jungryong had gazed down at the kneeling Park Tae Seop before asking him a single question.

[P115]
*If I help you, what can you do for me?*

[P116]
Park Tae Seop’s answer had come without hesitation.

[P117]
*I’ll do anything.*

[P118]
*I like that.*

[P119]
What would have happened if he had never said those words?

[P120]
He had asked himself that question hundreds, even thousands of times over the past twenty years, but there was no point. He had already come too far to turn back.

[P121]
There was no such thing as a favor without a price, and he had been forced to commit all kinds of crimes for Lee Jungryong.

[P122]
When he came to his senses, all he could see was himself being dragged along with a leash around his neck.

[P123]

[P124]
“How could that be?”

[P125]
“No. That’s simply how human beings are. Even when they receive a favor, they quickly forget their gratitude and do nothing but pile up complaints. Save a man who was about to freeze to death, and his attitude changes as soon as he warms himself by a campfire. What can you do? Ha ha.”

[P126]
“…….”

[P127]
Despite the corners of his mouth curling upward, Lee Jungryong’s eyes were as cold as ice.

[P128]
When Park Tae Seop lowered his head with a hardened expression, Lee Jungryong continued in a gentler voice.

[P129]
“I only said that so we could continue working well together in the future. Your Guild members will be safe as well, so don’t worry about anything. Isn’t that right, Team Leader Seok?”

[P130]

[P131]
“Of course.”

[P132]
“Well, then, I should be going. I’ll see you again.”

[P133]
Tap, tap.

[P134]
Park Tae Seop stood rigidly in place and watched Lee Jungryong’s back as he walked away after patting him on the shoulder.

[P135]
* * *

[P136]
Team Leader Seok spoke inside the descending elevator.

[P137]
“Shall I take care of him?”

[P138]
“Who? Ah, Park Tae Seop.”

[P139]
“Yes. His expression looked rather uneasy.”

[P140]
“That man’s thoughts are written all over his face. He was obedient for the first few years, but once he got comfortable and well-fed, he started entertaining other ideas.”

[P141]
“He knows too much. And he handled this incident so poorly that the fallout reached the Vice Guild Master.”

[P142]
For the first time, emotion entered Team Leader Seok’s voice.

[P143]
Anger.

[P144]
Lee Jungryong confirmed the steadfast loyalty he held toward him and smiled faintly.

[P145]
“Leave him for now. Besides, we’ve only just taken a taste, so of course it’s bland.”

[P146]
“Excuse me?”

[P147]
At that moment, the elevator doors opened with a ding.

[P148]
Lee Jungryong continued speaking as he walked.

[P149]
“I only gave things a little prod. I wanted to see what the response would be.”

[P150]
“Then…?”

[P151]
“You occasionally have a tendency to underestimate me. If I had made up my mind, would I have entrusted this work to such half-baked fools?”

[P152]
Team Leader Seok let out a low exclamation.

[P153]
“You anticipated all of this.”

[P154]
“I’ve only taken a spoonful and tasted it. If it doesn’t seem right, I can add salt and pepper.”

[P155]
“As expected of you, Vice Guild Master.”

[P156]
At the admiring look in Team Leader Seok’s eyes, Lee Jungryong smiled gently.

[P157]
But his thoughts were different. There was something he could not reveal even to Team Leader Seok, his right-hand man.

[P158]
*Jin Taekyung. He’s no ordinary man.*

[P159]
From the beginning, what had bothered Lee Jungryong was the Peace Guild, not Jin Taekyung.

[P160]
Even if he had stepped in himself, he could not guarantee that something like this would not have happened. He was not the sort of person who used a butcher’s knife to kill a chicken.

[P161]
It was certainly an efficient approach, but if an unexpected variable appeared, the plan would fall apart.

[P162]
*So there was a wolf hiding among the chickens.*

[P163]
Lee Jungryong rubbed his tingling wrist.

[P164]
For a moment, he had felt tremendous heat and power radiating from the young man. It was far too strong to dismiss as some fresh-faced brat’s cute little display.

[P165]
*He knew how to handle mana properly. A man who had been nothing more than an F-rank Hunter until recently—where on earth had he…?*

[P166]
There was one possibility he could reasonably guess at.

[P167]
After finishing his train of thought, Lee Jungryong said to Team Leader Seok,

[P168]
“Keep a close eye on Jin Taekyung.”

[P169]
“Don’t worry. If he becomes a problem, I’ll deal with him personally.”

[P170]
Team Leader Seok had always been reliable. He was a born fighting prodigy and the best among the children Lee Jungryong had personally selected and taught, so there was no need to question his skill. Even Park Tae Seop, a top-ranking ranker, was no match for him.

[P171]
But Lee Jungryong suddenly found himself wondering.

[P172]
Was Team Leader Seok really superior to Jin Taekyung?

[P173]
“Team Leader Seok. No, Go Jun.”

[P174]
His form of address had changed from a title to a name.

[P175]
Team Leader Seok was not the kind of person who would fail to understand what that meant. If he had lacked even that much awareness, he could never have become Lee Jungryong’s prized Disciple.

[P176]
“Yes, Master.”

[P177]
“Hmm. It’s nothing. I was entertaining a ridiculous thought for a moment.”

[P178]
Lee Jungryong clicked his tongue softly and walked out through the main entrance.

[P179]
Five men and women were waiting outside the building. They wore robes covered in elaborate patterns and carried staffs.

[P180]
“We greet the Vice Guild Master.”

[P181]
“Your outfits are certainly gaudy. Can’t you dress a little more ordinarily?”

[P182]
“They’ll look ordinary. To everyone else.”

[P183]
They were A-rank mages directly under Lee Jungryong.

[P184]
Just as the oldest-looking mage had said, none of the hundreds of people hurrying along the sidewalk paid them any attention.

[P185]
They did not even know that an incredible battle had taken place above their heads—one that had nearly brought down a high-rise building.

[P186]
“This is why magic is so convenient.”

[P187]
In a brute-force move, the mages had blanketed everything within a radius of roughly two hundred meters with an illusion spell. They could pull it off because they were A-rank mages of Ares Guild, which selected only the best.

[P188]
They would maintain the illusion spell here until all the cleanup was finished.

[P189]
“Yes. Use that convenient magic to handle things properly so no rumors come out of this. If anyone seems dangerous, use mental magic to tamper with their memories.”

[P190]
“Yes, sir. Understood. But that man is badly injured.”

[P191]
“Ah, him?”

[P192]
Lee Jungryong glanced at Park Jihoon, who was being carried on the back of one of the security team’s Hunters, and tossed out a single sentence.

[P193]
“Treat him just enough, then dump him somewhere.”

[P194]
If he died, so be it. Even if he recovered, he would not be able to properly use even half of the skill he currently possessed.

[P195]
Lee Jungryong had no hobby of collecting spent batteries. He already had countless batteries, and replacing one was all it took.

[P196]
*Still, he proved useful at the end.*

[P197]
Through Park Jihoon, Lee Jungryong had gotten a measure of Jin Taekyung’s ruthlessness.

[P198]
Once blood had been drawn, he should have killed him. If Lee Jungryong himself had been in that position, he would have done so without fail.

[P199]
*You couldn’t take that one step.*

[P200]

[P201]
*That half measure will come back to poison you someday.*

[P202]
Lee Jungryong let out a derisive chuckle and climbed into the car that was waiting for him.

“I only brought it up because I hope we’ll continue working well together. Your Guild members will be perfectly safe, so don’t worry. Isn’t that right, Team Leader Seok?”

[P131]
The middle-aged man responsible for Lee Jungryong’s security, Team Leader Seok, answered in a flat voice.

[P132]
“Of course.”

[P133]
“Well, I should be on my way. I’ll see you again.”

[P134]
Pat, pat.

[P135]
Park Tae Seop stood frozen as Lee Jungryong patted him on the shoulder and walked away.

[P136]
* * *

[P137]
Inside the descending elevator, Team Leader Seok spoke.

[P138]
“Shall I take care of him?”

[P139]
“Who? Ah, Park Tae Seop.”

[P140]
“Yes. The look on his face made me uneasy.”

[P141]
“That man’s every thought shows on his face. He was obedient enough for the first few years, but once he got warm and well-fed, he began entertaining other ideas.”

[P142]
“He knows too much. He also handled this incident so poorly that the fallout reached you, Vice Guild Master.”

[P143]
For the first time, emotion entered Team Leader Seok’s voice.

[P144]
Anger.

[P145]
Seeing the man’s unwavering loyalty, Lee Jungryong smiled faintly.

[P146]
“Leave him alone for now. We’ve only just started tasting the dish. Of course it’s still bland.”

[P147]
“Excuse me?”

[P148]
At that moment, the elevator doors opened with a ding.

[P149]
Lee Jungryong continued as he walked.

[P150]
“I’m saying I only gave them a little prod. I wanted to see how they would react.”

[P151]
“Then…?”

[P152]
“You occasionally underestimate me. If I had truly set my mind to it, would I have entrusted the job to half-baked fools like them?”

[P153]
Team Leader Seok let out a low exclamation.

[P154]
“You anticipated all of this.”

[P155]
“I’ve barely taken a single spoonful to taste it. If it doesn’t suit my palate, I can always add some salt and pepper.”

[P156]
“As expected of you, Vice Guild Master.”

[P157]
Lee Jungryong smiled gently at the admiration in Team Leader Seok’s eyes.

[P158]
But his true thoughts were different. There was something he couldn’t reveal even to Team Leader Seok, his right-hand man.

[P159]
*Jin Taekyung is no ordinary bastard.*

[P160]
From the beginning, it had been the Peace Guild that bothered Lee Jungryong, not Jin Taekyung.

[P161]
Even if he had personally intervened, he couldn’t guarantee that something like this wouldn’t have happened. After all, he wasn’t the sort of man who used a cleaver meant for cattle to kill a chicken.

[P162]
It was certainly efficient, but if an unforeseen variable appeared, the entire plan could go awry.

[P163]
*Who would’ve thought there was a wolf hiding among the chickens?*

[P164]
Lee Jungryong rubbed his tingling wrist.

[P165]
For a moment, he had felt tremendous heat and power from the brat. It had been far too strong to dismiss as a mere trick from some green youngster.

[P166]
*He knew how to control mana properly. Where could a man who was only an F-rank Hunter until recently have learned…?*

[P167]
He did have a fairly good idea.

[P168]
After finishing that thought, Lee Jungryong addressed Team Leader Seok.

[P169]
“Keep a close eye on Jin Taekyung.”

[P170]
“Don’t worry. If he becomes a nuisance, I’ll deal with him personally.”

[P171]
Team Leader Seok had always been reliable. He was a born fighting prodigy and the finest of all the youths Lee Jungryong had personally selected and trained. His skill was beyond question. Even a high-level ranker like Park Tae Seop was no match for him.

[P172]
But a question suddenly occurred to Lee Jungryong.

[P173]
Could Team Leader Seok really defeat Jin Taekyung?

[P174]
“Team Leader Seok. No, Go Jun.”

[P175]
His form of address had shifted from the man’s position to his name.

[P176]
Team Leader Seok understood the meaning immediately. If he had lacked even that much perception, he could never have become Lee Jungryong’s prized Disciple.

[P177]
“Yes, Master.”

[P178]
“Hmm. It’s nothing. I entertained an absurd thought for a moment.”

[P179]
Lee Jungryong clicked his tongue softly and walked through the main entrance.

[P180]
Five men and women were waiting outside the building, dressed in robes covered with elaborate patterns and carrying staffs.

[P181]
“We greet the Vice Guild Master.”

[P182]
“Those outfits are certainly gaudy. Can’t you dress a little more ordinarily?”

[P183]
“They’ll look ordinary to everyone else.”

[P184]
They were A-rank mages under Lee Jungryong’s direct command.

[P185]
Just as the oldest-looking mage had said, not one of the hundreds of people hurrying along the sidewalk paid them any attention.

[P186]
None of those people even knew that an incredible battle had taken place directly above them—one that had nearly brought down a high-rise building.

[P187]
“This is why magic is so convenient.”

[P188]
The mages had used brute force to blanket everything within a radius of roughly two hundred meters with illusion magic. Only the handpicked A-rank mages of Ares Guild could pull off something on that scale.

[P189]
They would remain there and maintain the illusion until the entire aftermath had been dealt with.

[P190]
“Good. Use that convenient magic of yours to make sure no rumors get out. If anyone looks dangerous, use mental magic to tamper with their memories.”

[P191]
“Yes, sir. Understood. But that man is badly injured.”

[P192]
“Ah, him?”

[P193]
Lee Jungryong glanced at Park Jihoon, who was being carried on the back of a Hunter from his security team, and casually tossed out an order.

[P194]
“Treat him just enough to keep him alive, then dump him somewhere.”

[P195]
If he died, so be it. Even if he recovered, he would never again be able to display half his current strength.

[P196]
Lee Jungryong had no interest in collecting spent batteries. He already had countless others. All he had to do was replace this one.

[P197]
*Still, he was useful at the end.*

[P198]
Through Park Jihoon, Lee Jungryong had confirmed the extent of Jin Taekyung’s ruthlessness.

[P199]
Once blood had been spilled, he should have killed him. Lee Jungryong would certainly have done so.

[P200]
*You couldn’t take that final step.*

[P201]
What did it matter if he cut off both arms and carved the man’s body to pieces? As long as his enemy still drew breath, it wasn’t complete revenge.

[P202]
It was nothing more than venting his anger.

[P203]
*That half-measure will come back to poison you someday.*

[P204]
Lee Jungryong let out a derisive chuckle and climbed into the waiting car.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
